Hon'ble Jaspreet Singh,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. This Court by means of its order dated 27.05.2024 had passed the following order which reads as under:-
"Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.

The instant application has been filed seeking pre-arrest bail in FIR/Case Crime No.0014/2023, under Sections 409, 420, 467, 468, 201, 204, 166 and 120-B IPC,
Lalman vs State Of U.P. Thru.

1 relating to police station SIT, Lucknow.

The submission of the learned counsel for the applicant is that an FIR came to be lodged on 10.03.2023 wherein primarily the allegations were that certain officials of the Minority Welfare Department without making proper scrutiny and spot verification released funds in respect of certain Madarsas which were not existing and thus the release of the Government funds have been misappropriated.

The further submission of the learned counsel for the applicant is that insofar as the present applicant is concerned, he was subjected to departmental enquiry in respect of identical charge wherein it was found that only against eight such Madarsas,
proper scrutiny was not done and this fact apart it was based on the reports submitted by the other officials and the applicant himself was not squarely responsible.

It is further submitted that even in the departmental enquiry, the role of the applicant was not found substantiated, however, since the applicant was working in tandem with other officials, consequently, he was let off with warning.

It has further been urged that despite the said order, the applicant assailed the same before this Court in WRIT-A No.2631 of 2023 wherein by means of the order dated 07.04.2023, the Court had granted indulgence and the order impugned dated 12.05.2022 was stayed.

It is also urged the subsequently once again departmental enquiry was initiated against the applicant on the same charge and the applicant was put under suspension which again become the subject matter of WRIT-A No.8423 of 2023 wherein a Coordinate Bench of this Court by means of the order dated 29.05.2023 had stayed the aforesaid suspension order, however, liberty was granted to conclude the proceedings.
The submission of the learned counsel for the applicant is that till date the enquiry has not been concluded.
It has further been urged that the applicant has deep roots in the society.
He is the District Welfare Minority Officer and he has no chance of fleeing justice or in a position either to tamper with the evidence or influence the witness.

It is further urged that the applicant is ready to cooperate in context with the fact that the FIR has been lodged in the year 2023 and till date there is no incriminating material found against the applicant nor the custody of the applicant has been sought for any interrogation.
In such circumstances, in order to humiliate the applicant, he has now been impending threat of being arrested by the police authorities.
In the aforesaid circumstances, the applicant is entitled for protection under Section 438 Lalman vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. /Addl. ...

on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131376173/
2 Cr.P.C.
Learned AGA submits that he requires time to file his objections as well as seek his complete instructions.

Let a counter affidavit be filed by the learned AGA within a period of three weeks with an advance copy to the learned counsel for the applicant, who if may so choose, may file his response thereto within a further period of ten days.
List this matter on 09.07.2024.
3. By means of the said order interim protection was granted to the applicant, in the meantime, the State was directed to file its counter-affidavit.
4. The record further indicates that the counter-affidavit and rejoinder-affidavit have been exchanged between the parties.
5. Primary submission of the learned A.G.A. is that the applicant was part of the committee who had granted the recognition to certain Madarsas which were found to be non-existent.

A specific pinpointed query was put to the learned A.G.A. to indicate from the material on record as to what is the material against the applicant by which it can be, prima facie, noticed that the applicant apart from being a member of the committee was required to discharge his duties of physically verifying the Madarsas despite the report of the inspector.
It could not be pointed out that the applicant was under any obligation to verify the report submitted physically.

All what has been said in the counter-affidavit filed by the State is that the applicant was a member of three persons committee who had relied upon the report of the inspector and had granted the conditional recognition that in case if any of the facts indicated were found to be false, the recognition would automatically stands cancelled.
Lalman vs State Of U.P. Thru.

6. Considering the aforesaid as well as the fact that the applicant is a public servant and has no criminal history.
7. This Court finds it a fit case to allow the present anticipatory bail in terms of the earlier order dated 27.05.2024 which is made abolute.
The anticipatory bail application is allowed.
9. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

10. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
